title: Iterates of the Weil $!$-pushforward
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, a finite field $k_0$ with $q$ elements and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $c\geq1$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^c$, with the finite-coefficient categories and derived operations of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be its base change. Let $\Phi_X,\Phi_Y$ be the base changes to $k$ of the $q$-power scheme Frobenii of $X_0,Y_0$ [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For every integer $j\geq1$, let
$$\theta_{f,j,K}:L\Phi_Y^{j*}Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf_!L\Phi_X^{j*}K$$
be the specified Frobenius comparison (compact-support exchange followed by the relative-Frobenius adjunction unit and the proper/direct-image and pullback composition comparisons) of [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward]. Let $m,n\geq1$.

1. *Base-change composition.* After the pullback composition
identifications $L\Phi^{(m+n)*}\simeq L\Phi^{m*}L\Phi^{n*}$ on $X$
and on $Y$,
$$
\theta_{f,m+n,K}=\theta_{f,m,L\Phi_X^{n*}K}\circ
L\Phi_Y^{m*}\theta_{f,n,K}:
L\Phi_Y^{(m+n)*}Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf_!L\Phi_X^{(m+n)*}K .
$$
1. *Iterates.* Let $u:L\Phi_X^*K\to K$ be a Frobenius coefficient
morphism, with iterates $u_m$ of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], and let
$\psi=Rf_!u\circ\theta_{f,1}$ be the Weil $!$-pushforward. Then the
iterates $\psi_m$ of the Frobenius coefficient morphism $\psi$ on
$Rf_!K$ satisfy
$$
\psi_m=Rf_!u_m\circ\theta_{f,m}\qquad(m\geq1).
$$

Neither statement uses invertibility of $u$.

proof.text: Work throughout at the fixed finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,c}$, with the separated finite-type geometric schemes of [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward]. The constructible domains in [prop-functor-package] contain $K$, its displayed pullbacks, and the compact-support direct images used below. In particular these objects are bounded with constructible cohomology. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], choose their bounded etale-origin witnesses when applying [fix-lem-exchanges]. Its finite-coefficient pasting formulas are therefore applicable; no completed or rational coefficient category is being identified with this category. Put $P=Lp_n^*K$ and $M=Lr_n^*P=L\Phi_X^{n*}K$ using the pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

source.place: Proof, Step 2: domains of the comparison and of its exchange transformations

proof.text:
Use the current defining display and projection identities of [d-relative-frob]: $X'_j=Y\times_{\Phi_Y^j,Y,f}X$, $r_j=(f,\Phi_X^j)$, $p_jr_j=\Phi_X^j$, $f'_jr_j=f$, and $\Phi_Y^jf=f\Phi_X^j$ for $j\geq1$. Its fibre product is the universal pair construction, so the following coordinate argument concerns scheme morphisms on every test scheme; it does not use the affine-chart paragraph of that node. In nested coordinates identify $X'_{m+n}$ with $Y\times_{\Phi_Y^m,Y,f'_n}X'_n$: a test-scheme point is $(y,(z,x'))$ with $z=\Phi_Y^m y$ and $f(x')=\Phi_Y^n z$. This is naturally equivalent to the pair $(y,x')$ with $f(x')=\Phi_Y^{m+n}y$. Write $q(y,(z,x'))=(z,x')$; then $p_{m+n}=p_nq$. Define $t:X'_m\to X'_{m+n}$ by $t(y,x)=(y,(f(x),\Phi_X^n x))$. The defining equations hold because $f(x)=\Phi_Y^m y$ and $f\Phi_X^n=\Phi_Y^n f$. For every test scheme, a point of $X'_{m+n}\times_{X'_n,r_n}X$ consists exactly of $(y,x)$ with $\Phi_Y^m y=f(x)$; the projections are $t$ and $p_m$. Thus the square with top $p_m$, bottom $q$, and vertical maps $t,r_n$ is Cartesian, as a functorial fibre-product identity, including for nonreduced test schemes. Also $f'_{m+n}t=f'_m$ and
$$t r_m(x)=(f(x),(f(\Phi_X^m x),\Phi_X^{m+n}x))=(f(x),(\Phi_Y^m f(x),\Phi_X^{m+n}x)),$$
which is $r_{m+n}(x)$ under the nested-coordinate identification. By [i-relative-frob], $r_n,r_m,r_{m+n}$ are finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), $t$ is finite. These finite maps are proper: apply its clause (c) to the identity of the target (which is proper directly from its definition). Hence their ordinary and compact-support direct images may be identified as in [prop-functor-package](3).

source.place: Proof, Step 1: factorization and Cartesian t-square; corrected nested coordinate of t r_m

proof.text:
Here is the unit calculation needed for that square. Write $\beta_Q:Lq^*Rr_{n*}Q\to Rt_*Lp_m^*Q$ for its ordinary exchange, as defined in [def-exchange-projection]. The adjunctions are supplied by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and the square comparison $\alpha:Lt^*Lq^*\simeq Lp_m^*Lr_n^*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Transpose $\beta_{Lr_n^*P}\circ Lq^*\eta_{r_n,P}$ under $Lt^*\dashv Rt_*$. The counit definition of exchange and naturality of $\alpha$ give the transpose
$$Lp_m^*\bigl(\varepsilon_{r_n,Lr_n^*P}\circ Lr_n^*\eta_{r_n,P}\bigr)\circ\alpha_P=\alpha_P,$$
by the triangle identity. The transpose of $Rt_*(\alpha_P)\circ\eta_{t,Lq^*P}$ is also $\alpha_P$. Injectivity of the adjunction hom bijection therefore proves
$$\beta_{Lr_n^*P}\circ Lq^*\eta_{r_n,P}=Rt_*(\alpha_P)\circ\eta_{t,Lq^*P}.$$
After the indicated pullback identification, this is precisely the unit $\eta_t$ on $N=Lq^*P$. This calculation needs neither an inverse of $\beta$ nor invertibility of a coefficient morphism.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: first two remaining arrows; Stacks 07A6 lemma-adjoint and 07A7 remark-base-change

proof.text:
For clarity also fix the composition normalization of units. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], the unit of $Lr_m^*Lt^*\dashv Rt_*Rr_{m*}$ at $N$ is
$$Rt_*(\eta_{r_m,Lt^*N})\circ\eta_{t,N}.$$
Under $r_{m+n}=tr_m$, the pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and the canonical direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identify this unit with $\eta_{r_{m+n},N}$. Indeed the composite hom bijection sends the identity of $Lr_m^*Lt^*N$ first to $\eta_{r_m,Lt^*N}$ and then to the displayed map. This is the canonical comparison just cited, rather than a choice of an unnormalized isomorphism: by [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], the derived hom bijection on a fraction representative is the class of the termwise adjoint map followed by its resolution comparisons. For a K-injective $I$ and a resolution $j:r_{m*}I\to J$, successively taking these adjoints inserts exactly the map $t_*j$; its class is the normalization of the direct-image composition node. The pullback comparison is likewise termwise on the K-flat representative by its cited statement. Thus the normalized comparison identifies this same bijection with the adjunction for $L(tr_m)^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; consequently it sends that identity to $\eta_{tr_m,N}$. This also fixes the direction of every composition comparison used here. For three pullbacks, their canonical comparisons agree because on a K-flat representative with flat terms each is the termwise composition comparison; both parenthesizations have the same action on every local section.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: composite-adjunction unit and canonical comparisons; Stacks 0DV0 lemma-compose-counits, 0D6D lemma-derived-pullback-composition, 0D6E lemma-derived-pushforward-composition

proof.text:
Expand $\theta_{f,m,M}\circ L\Phi_Y^{m*}\theta_{f,n,K}$ by [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward]. Each expansion consists of compact-support exchange, direct image of the relative-Frobenius unit, and the proper/direct-image and pullback composition identifications. The $\Phi_Y^m$ square for $f=f'_nr_n$ is the vertical pasting of the $t$-square in step 2 and the $\Phi_Y^m$ square for $f'_n$. By [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4), replace its exchange by that of $f'_n$ followed by the exchange for $r_n$ along $q$. The latter is $\beta$: since $r_n$ is proper, take the compactification $(\operatorname{id},r_n)$ in the formula of [def-exchange-projection]; the open exchange is the identity, so its compact-support formula is the ordinary exchange. Independence of this choice is [fix-lem-exchanges](4). Naturality in the coefficient morphism $\eta_{r_n,P}$, clause (1), moves the exchange for $f'_n$ past this unit. The two resulting exchanges for base changes $\Phi_Y^n$ and $\Phi_Y^m$ combine by clause (2) into the exchange for their outer rectangle. After that first arrow, the remaining map, before applying $Rf'_{m+n!}$, is
$$N\xrightarrow{Lq^*\eta_{r_n,P}}Lq^*Rr_{n*}Lr_n^*P\xrightarrow{\beta}Rt_*Lp_m^*Lr_n^*P\simeq Rt_*Lt^*N\xrightarrow{Rt_*\eta_{r_m,Lt^*N}}Rt_*Rr_{m*}Lr_m^*Lt^*N.$$
Step 3 identifies the first two arrows with $\eta_t$; step 4 identifies the whole map with $\eta_{r_{m+n},N}$. Thus this is the defining unit arrow of $\theta_{f,m+n,K}$. The remaining comparisons agree by the identity/associativity and coherence assertions of [prop-functor-package](3) and its final paragraph, together with the pullback comparisons of step 4: their composites are $f'_{m+n}tr_m=f$ and $p_nqtr_m=\Phi_X^{m+n}$. We have proved clause (1), as an equality of the specified maps, not just existence of an isomorphism between their endpoints.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: expand, paste, and identify the comparison

proof.text:
Prove clause (2) by induction on the positive integer $m$. The base $m=1$ is $\psi=Rf_!u\circ\theta_{f,1}$ from [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward]. Suppose $\psi_m=Rf_!u_m\circ\theta_{f,m,K}$. The recursion in the current statement of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] is specified for indices at least 2, with the separate base case at 1. Since $m\geq1$ here, it applies at $m+1$ and gives
$$\psi_{m+1}=Rf_!u\circ\theta_{f,1,K}\circ L\Phi_Y^*Rf_!u_m\circ L\Phi_Y^*\theta_{f,m,K}.$$
Apply the naturality of $\theta_{f,1}$ in [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward], whose current statement explicitly composes the naturality squares for its three defining arrows, to the actual morphism $u_m:L\Phi_X^{m*}K\to K$:
$$\theta_{f,1,K}\circ L\Phi_Y^*Rf_!u_m=Rf_!L\Phi_X^*u_m\circ\theta_{f,1,L\Phi_X^{m*}K}.$$
Functoriality of $Rf_!$, the recursion $u_{m+1}=u\circ L\Phi_X^*u_m$, and clause (1) proved in step 5 for $(1,m)$ now give
$$\psi_{m+1}=Rf_!u_{m+1}\circ\theta_{f,1,L\Phi_X^{m*}K}\circ L\Phi_Y^*\theta_{f,m,K}=Rf_!u_{m+1}\circ\theta_{f,m+1,K}.$$
This proves the induction. Every use of $u$ was composition or functoriality; no inverse was used, so the argument includes noninvertible and zero coefficient morphisms.
